analysis:
All units in this batch are test-only changes, and none of them alters a production control.

MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngineTests.swift head lines 625-634 add a test of ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope. It checks that GPT-OSS client stop strings are scoped to the Harmony final channel, by model id or by model_type gpt_oss. It also checks that Gemma and Qwen models get a nil scope.

NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift head lines 50-71 add a TextSession fixture. Head lines 94-116 add a test asserting that native-block requests carry no reasoning stop scope: stops match over the whole output, including reasoning text, and the matched stop is reported via EngineV2RequestUsageSignal.matchedStopSequence.

GemmaToolCallLiveTests.swift line 264 adds a .logprobs event case. This implies a new logprobs stream event in production code that is not supplied here.

Security relevance:
- Stop-string scoping changes how reasoning and final-channel text is truncated. This affects output correctness (T-007 class, but the operator is still the adversary) and not confidentiality.
- The native-block path stopping inside reasoning text matches the documented behavior; it is no regression.
- The new logprobs event may expose token probabilities to consumers. Integration should confirm that logprobs are emitted only when the request asks for them, and are encrypted on the coordinator leg like other chunks (T-008 fail-closed encryption). They should also not be exposed for hidden reasoning tokens or leak cross-request data (T-041/T-028 timing and cache channels are not affected by these tests).

No production source was supplied, so these are integration questions rather than findings.
